fields.h1: Build a Youth Sports Registration Form That Places Every Player
fields.hero_description: Get a youth sports registration form that sets each player's age group and saves every family to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Everything a Season Needs Before Practice Starts
fields.features_subheading: Paper packets ask for the same parent details once per child. This form asks once per family, then places and prices every player.
fields.feature_1:
Age groups worked out from the birth year

Tell the form which birth years play in which group, such as 2016 and 2017 in 10U. A parent enters the birth date, and the player's group shows on screen before the parent submits.
fields.feature_2:
One checkout for the whole family

A parent adds every child to one registration, even across sports. The form applies your sibling price, and the app takes one card payment through the Stripe account you connect.
fields.feature_3:
Waivers signed before the form submits

Put the participation waiver and your code of conduct on the last page. A parent types or draws a signature there, and the form will not submit until that signature is in place.
fields.feature_4:
Rosters coaches can open on a phone

Coaches see their own team and no other, with a parent phone number and an emergency contact for each player. Nobody has to forward a spreadsheet the night before practice.
fields.feature_5:
Every family in a table you own

Registrations land in a database you own, and the form has no response caps for a busy spring signup. Last season's families stay in the table when the next season opens.
fields.feature_6:
The full code in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the code to your GitHub repository if the league's website lives there. Keep building on it yourself, or keep asking Emergent for changes in plain English.

fields.usecase_heading: One Fall Season at Thistle Creek Recreation
fields.tab_content_1:
For a 2017 birth year, the form picks 10U

Thistle Creek Recreation groups its fall soccer players by birth year, and players born in 2016 or 2017 play in 10U. Sabela Kimball enters her son Zuriel's birth date, March 3, 2017. The form shows 10U before she submits, and her confirmation email names the group and the first practice on September 8.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each sibling after the first costs $75

Leocadia Vasquez-Tull has three children to register, two for fall soccer and one for flag football. Thistle Creek charges $95 for the first player and $75 for each sibling, whatever the sport. She adds all three to one form and pays $245 once through Stripe. Each child lands on the roster for their own sport.
fields.tab_content_3:
No payment step when a family asks for help

Isadora Sternhagen checks the fee assistance box when she registers her daughter for flag football. The form skips the payment page and marks the registration Pending review. Treasurer Ottilie Pemberley gets an email to approve it. The coach sees the player on the team roster with no fee details.
fields.tab_content_4:
Wrenna orders 80 jerseys from one count

Thistle Creek's fall soccer has 80 players, and each parent picked a jersey size on the form. Registration closes on August 15, and equipment coordinator Wrenna Meriwether opens the dashboard the next morning. She orders from the count: 18 youth small, 31 youth medium, 22 youth large, and 9 adult small.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Youth Sports Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a youth sports registration form that places every player in a group and gets each family paid in one checkout.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List each program and its age groups
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only for what coaches use
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the waiver on the last page
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every sport you run this season and the birth years each age group takes, such as 2014 and 2015 in 12U. Keep a separate list for any sport whose groups differ.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Set the first-player fee and the sibling price, and decide whether a brother or sister in another sport counts as a sibling. Add a fee assistance option for families who need one.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the player's name, birth date, sport, and jersey size. Then add the contacts a coach calls on game day, and leave off any question nobody on the board will read.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste your participation waiver and code of conduct onto the final page, with a signature box under each. Use the wording your league already has; the form collects the signature.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the programs and fees into one prompt, along with the fields. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and a dashboard for the registrar. Change a question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect Stripe and pick who hears
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect your Stripe account so a family pays once at checkout. Then pick who gets an email when a parent asks for fee assistance, such as the treasurer.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign up one child alone, then a family of three, then a fee assistance request. Check the age group on each confirmation, the sibling total, and the email to the treasurer.

faq_plan.q: What is a youth sports registration form?
faq_plan.a: A youth sports registration form is the sign-up a parent fills in to put a child on a team for a season. It records the player's name, birth date, and sport, how to reach the parent, and a signed waiver. The registrar uses it to place each player in a group and build the rosters.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a youth sports registration form?
faq_plan.a: Write down your programs and age groups, what each family pays, and the questions coaches need answered. Put that list into a single prompt for Emergent's AI form builder, and it returns the form with the database behind it. Then sign up a pretend family yourself before the link goes out to parents.

faq_plan.q: Is a youth sports registration form template enough for a rec league season?
faq_plan.a: It can be, if the template matches how your season works. Before you use one, check three things: it places players by birth year, it prices siblings the way your board does, and it takes payment. Emergent builds those rules into the form from a plain-English description, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: When does baseball need a separate form from the youth sports registration form?
faq_plan.a: When the baseball program places players by league age or checks where each family lives, give it a separate little league registration form. Those rules do not apply to your other sports. A rec program that groups every sport by birth year can keep baseball on the same form as soccer.

faq_plan.q: What should a youth sports registration form ask parents?
faq_plan.a: Start with the player: sport, full name, birth date, and jersey size. Then take a parent phone number, an emergency contact, and a signature on the waiver, plus a fee assistance checkbox if you offer help with fees. Emergent builds the form on a database you own, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a sibling discount to a youth sports registration form?
faq_plan.a: Set a fee for the first child and a lower price for each brother or sister, then let a parent add every child to one form. Before the form opens, decide whether a sibling in another sport still counts and whether the sibling price applies on top of fee assistance. Write both answers on the payment page.

faq_plan.q: Can one youth sports registration form cover both a season and a tournament?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep them on separate forms. A season form signs up one child at a time for weeks of practices and games. A weekend event signs up whole teams with an entry fee, which is the job of a tournament registration form. Link the two from your league's website so families pick the right one.

faq_plan.q: How far ahead of the season should a youth sports registration form open?
faq_plan.a: Open it about 8 weeks before the first practice and close it 3 weeks out. That leaves time to build teams and to order jerseys from the final count. Put the closing date at the top of the form. The app can email reminders to last season's families on the dates you choose.

faq_plan.q: How should a youth sports registration form handle families who cannot afford the fee?
faq_plan.a: Offer fee assistance on the form itself: a checkbox that skips the payment page and sends the request to one person, such as the treasurer. Keep the request off coach rosters. Agree on the rules before the form opens, whether that is a full waiver or a reduced fee. The app emails the treasurer as each request comes in.

faq_plan.q: Can a youth sports registration form work for a summer sports camp?
faq_plan.a: Not well. Give a camp its own form. A camp signs a child up by the week and asks for daily pickup details. A summer camp registration form is built around both. Your season form places players in an age group for a full schedule of games, and its fields stay focused on that.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook for this Wave 3 keyword; the searcher is a rec department or club registrar running a youth season. This page wins by showing Emergent building the jobs a multi-sport youth season adds: placing each player in an age group by birth year, one checkout for siblings across sports with a sibling price, a private fee assistance request that skips payment and reaches only the treasurer, and a jersey size count the equipment coordinator orders from. Distinct from the Little League page (league age, residency) and the tournament page (team caps, entry fees).

findings.quote: A form template stops at names and phone numbers.
findings.issue: False differentiator: youth sports registration templates from the vendors in the table below routinely include payment fields and conditional logic, and the page itself says in FAQ 3 that a template 'can be' enough if it places players, prices siblings and takes payment. The page contradicts itself and makes an untrue claim about competitors' templates. Search of the page found no other instance (the plan.angle carries the same unsourced idea: 'registration templates stop at player name, parent contact and a signature line'; plan is not rendered).
findings.fix: Say what Emergent builds without a claim about templates, e.g. 'Describe your age groups and sibling prices once, and Emergent builds them into the form itself.'
